Now, here already on the 30th of June, 1992, you see the Security Council calling on Croatia to withdraw and to cease hostile military activities in or near the UNPAs; correct?

utterances.speaker: RATKO LICINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, but Croatia did not act upon this. And it was not sanctioned, it was not penalised for such a flagrant violation of international law.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honour, could this be admitted into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes Exhibit number 882.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: And if we could see another United Nations Security Council resolution. This one has the ERN DK00-3845 to 3846. This is Resolution 802 from the 25th of January, 1993. If we could scroll down, please, where it says "deeply concerned." There. That's fine. Mr. Licina, here the Security Council says that it was: "Deeply concerned by information provided by the Secretary-General to the Security Council on 25 January, 1993, on the rapid and violent deterioration in the situation in Croatia as a result of military attacks by Croatian armed forces on the areas under the protection of the United Nations Protection Force ..." And then it says it: "Strongly condemns those attacks which have led to casualties and loss of life in UNPROFOR, as well as among the civilian population." Here the United Nations Security Council is strongly condemning one of those Croatian attacks; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: RATKO LICINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's exactly what I've been testifying about. Croatia committed aggression after aggression on the territory of the Serbian Krajina, a territory protected by the United Nations, whereas the Security Council reacted only with strong-worded communiques and nothing else. I agree with what you just read. It's correct what you read. However, Croatia did not suffer any sanctions on that occasion. I'm not saying the resolutions were not issued, but there was no practical result, practical outcome of these resolutions. You saw that there was one resolution in June, 1991. The same thing happened in January, 1992, and again the Security Council gave them a rap on the knuckles. I'm not saying the resolutions did not exist, but they produced nothing in practice. The only result was another aggression against another territory protected by the United Nations. That's what I'm saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: And what you said yesterday, or perhaps it was the day before, was that it -- "The UN practically encouraged" these Croatian operations. But that's not right, is it?

utterances.speaker: RATKO LICINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: If after the first aggression against the UNPA Croatia did not suffer strong sanctions and was not punished, it was natural that their authorities, their government, saw it as an encouragement for further aggressions, because they did not -- they were not subjected to any stronger sanctions than a reprimand by the United Nations. Did peace troops come to Zagreb? Did anything else happen? No. It just remained an empty word on a paper.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Well, in fact, peace troops came to the -- they were already in the United Nations Protected Areas; right? Croatia already had a United Nations peacekeeping force on its territory. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: RATKO LICINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were peacekeeping forces in the territory of the Serbian Krajina. Croatia committed an aggression against that area protected by the United Nations. In fact, several aggressions. And each time the only response to that were these resolutions. Croatia was not subjected to any other sanction. That's what I'm saying. And if we go on this way, it will go on until tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: None of these places -- well, all of these places, Miljevac plateau, Maslenica, Medak pocket, those were the so-called pink zones. They weren't inside the United Nations Protected Areas, were they?

utterances.speaker: RATKO LICINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not true. Those areas were also protected by the United Nations. There were UN troops in Medak and that area was certainly protected by the UN.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: There were -- let me interrupt you. There were -- there may have been UN patrols there, but these were areas that were part of Croatia. These weren't part of the SAO Krajina. These were areas that it was always stated that Croatia would reassert its control over these so-called pink zones. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: RATKO LICINA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm out of time for today. May I admit this into evidence and then that will be it for today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will become Exhibit number 883.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The Court will now adjourn for the day. We'll reconvene tomorrow at 9.00 in the same court. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 17th day of August, 2006, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.45 p.m.,
